params.body:
The last piece of the logging work. A vehicle carries eight prices and every one of them is a current value: a save overwrites it and the number that stood there is gone.

That is why three questions a dealer platform exists to answer could not be answered at all — not because the sums are hard, but because there is nothing to sum:

- does lowering an asking price actually sell the car
- how long does a dealer wait before he lowers it
- how much comes off between asking and sold

One row per price that moved: which vehicle, which field, from what to what, when, and by whom.

## Its own table, not the event log

`activity_events` counts how much people do. A price change is a field-level fact with two sides to it, and folding two shapes into one table makes both awkward to read. Volume is a subset of the saves, so it stays well under the event log, which is itself a fifth of `vehicle_photos` per year.

## Four decisions worth stating

**Only on a change, never on creation.** A price going from nothing to a number is where a history starts, not a change within it; logging it would put a row against every vehicle ever entered, for a question nobody asks.

**Rewriting the same number is not a change.** Eloquent sees `"12500"` and `12500.0` as different, so without a comparison to the cent every save of an untouched sheet wrote seven rows.

**Two prices in one save are two rows.** A margin moves when the purchase price and the repairs move together, and one row per save would hide which of the two did it.

**A price moved without a person still counts.** This is where it deliberately differs from the event log, which skips machine saves because it asks how much *people* work. A price an import or a scheduled command changed is still a price that changed, and the empty user column says it was not a person.

`flexlease_starting_price` stays out: a scheduled command derives it from the other prices, so its history would be a shadow of theirs.

## Verified

Seven tests, one per decision above plus the two that always apply: an unwritable table does not break saving a car, and the derived lease price has no history.

New rule R S1-9.25 — .20 was taken, so this took the next free number in that functionality. `phpstan` green, `pint` green on the added files. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment; CI runs on a fresh database.

## No screen yet, on purpose

Like the event log and the page counter, this starts empty. A price timeline on a vehicle sheet, or an average discount across the fleet, is worth building once there is a few weeks of it to show — and by then it will be clear which of the three questions above is the one actually being asked.
params.title: A price has a history
